Kitchen, meals & drinks

cooking pot noun

also pot, casserole, stockpot

classical

M-O s.v. pan: pot (cacabus)
Varro
Stat. Silv. 4.9.45

1Why caccabus, not cācabus: the word is Greek κάκκαβος, with a short α and a double κ. Varro writes caccabum (Lewis & Short), and Statius scans albōrum calicum atque caccabōrum (Silv. 4.9.45) with a heavy first syllable, which the double c explains. Lewis & Short prints cācabus, marking that heavy syllable as a long vowel. Comenius’s cacabīs is marked to match. Ruling: caccabus: a short a and a double c (provisional).

caccabus1 (cacabus), caccabī m.

noun, second declension

Examples

  • ēlixat ōllīs et cacabīs in focō

    he boils in pots and pans on the hearthComen. OP 54

See also saucepan.

SourcesLewis & Short: cacabus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pan: saucepan, pan: pot, cutlery: spoon: slotted spoon, sieve, sieve: colander, grater: cheese-grater, wire whisk, press: garlic press.

Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
